Effects.evidence_source: No correlation coefficients between intelligence and creative achievement were explicitly reported in the text for the current study.

Measure IQ.evidence_source: Fluid intelligence was assessed using a 17-item subsample of Sandia Matrices (Matzen et al., 2010).

IQ modality.evidence_source: The Sandia Matrices are nonverbal object relations (i.e., involving one, two, or three transformations) and logic (i.e., conjunction and disjunction) problems similar to those used in the popular Raven's Progressive Matrices (Raven, Raven, & Court, 1998).

IQ Aspect.evidence_source: Fluid intelligence was assessed using a 17-item subsample of Sandia Matrices (Matzen et al., 2010).

Creativity Measures.evidence_source: Creative achievement was assessed using the Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ; Carson, Peterson, & Higgins, 2005).

Domain classified.evidence_source: Scores were totaled to create an overall Creative Achievement score as well as a score specific to the arts and a score specific to the sciences. Domains assigned to the arts and sciences were consistent with Kaufman et al. (2016): Arts included Visual Arts, Music, Dance, Creative Writing, Humor, and Theater/Film, whereas Science included Inventions and Scientific Discovery.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the measures and scoring methods for creative achievement, intelligence, and personality used in the present study. Creative achievement was assessed using the Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ), yielding an overall score and scores specific to arts and sciences. Fluid intelligence was measured with a 17-item subsample of Sandia Matrices, described as nonverbal problems. The section also discusses the application of IRT scoring for intelligence and personality, along with model-data fit and reliability assessments.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the measures and scoring methods for creative achievement, intelligence, and personality. Creative achievement was assessed using the Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ), yielding overall, arts-specific, and science-specific scores. Fluid intelligence was measured with nonverbal Sandia Matrices, and personality was assessed using an ideal-point measure of openness to experience. Item response theory (IRT) scoring was applied to intelligence and personality measures, with model-data fit and marginal reliability statistics presented in Table 1.
